description: We are OPTIMUS, computer engineering students from Yaounde passionate about data, AI and Earth observation. We are tackling the MODIS/VIIRS hotspot challenge: a web app that harmonizes 20+ years of satellite fire data into a burning-activity calendar, with a focus on Central Africa’s seasonal fires. We bring data engineering, ML/forecasting and full-stack skills. Looking for: front-end & data viz, design & storytelling, and Earth science profiles. Join us!
summary: Ember turns 25 years of NASA FIRMS active-fire hotspots into one consistent burning-activity calendar. MODIS (2000-) and VIIRS (2012-) cannot be compared directly: VIIRS's 375 m pixels detect 3 to 5 times more hotspots, which creates an artificial jump in 2012 and hides real trends. Ember counts every detection on a common 0.1° grid per month, then calibrates MODIS onto the VIIRS scale with transfer factors fitted per cell on the 2012-2025 overlap, with an uncertainty band and held-out validation. A web app lets emergency managers draw an area and see a year x month calendar, the fire-season onset and peak, the most active years, and whether the current month is above or below its historical median. The last 60 days come live from the FIRMS API through the same pipeline and are flagged provisional. We processed the full global MODIS archive (102.7 million detections). For Cameroon, October 2026 already runs at 1.65 times its historical median: the fire season is starting early and strong.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Ember answers three questions for a selected area: which months of the year burn the most, which years were exceptional, and is the current month unusual compared with the past. Users draw a rectangle or polygon on a map (or type coordinates), pick a period, and get:

- a year x month burning-activity calendar with an accessible color ramp (viridis), where reconstructed and provisional months are marked;

- the current or any chosen month compared with the same month in every past year (ratio to the median, percentile, plain-language label);

- the fire season onset, peak and end, and the most active years;

- a monthly series with an uncertainty band, a seasonal profile with the 25th-75th percentile range, and a map of active grid cells;

- a CSV export, and a public REST API for other tools.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Filter: MODIS confidence >= 30, VIIRS nominal or high confidence, vegetation fires only (static sources, volcanoes and offshore detections removed).

2. Grid: each detection is counted on 0.1° cells (about 11 km) per month and per platform (Terra, Aqua, Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20). Cells absorb the footprint and geolocation differences between 1 km MODIS and 375 m VIIRS pixels.

3. Calibrate: on the 2012-2025 overlap, a transfer factor k = VIIRS / MODIS is fitted per cell, falling back to 1° blocks and then to a global factor where data is sparse. Aqua and Suomi-NPP share the 13:30 overpass, which isolates the sensor effect.

4. One record: VIIRS months are used as observed; earlier MODIS months are multiplied by k. The year-to-year spread of k gives an uncertainty band.

5. Validate: factors fitted on 2012-2018 predict 2019-2025. On synthetic data with a known 4x gap, the bias ratio goes from 0.25 (raw) to 1.00 (harmonized). The same validation runs on real data as soon as the VIIRS archive ingestion completes.

6. Live: the last 60 days are fetched from the FIRMS area API, aggregated by the same code, scaled with the stored factors and flagged provisional. Without calibration, the app uses MODIS near-real-time data, which is on the same scale as the MODIS archive.

STATUS

The full global MODIS archive (5,275 FIRMS files, 102.7 million detections, 2000-2025) was processed on Kaggle in 30 minutes into 19.2 million cell-months on 799,550 grid cells. Any area is answered in under one second. Live data is connected and working. VIIRS S-NPP and NOAA-20 archives are being ingested to run the real calibration.

TOOLS

Python (pandas, pyarrow, NumPy), FastAPI, Leaflet, Chart.js, Streamlit prototype, Kaggle notebooks for the global run, NASA FIRMS archive and API, automated unit and API tests. Open source on GitHub.

IMPACT AND CREATIVITY

Emergency responders and land managers get a consistent 25-year baseline instead of two incompatible records, so a "high" month means high compared with history, not compared with an older, less sensitive sensor. Suomi-NPP stopped on 2 November 2026 and MODIS is near end of life: harmonization is what keeps the record usable. We chose a transparent, explainable method (ratios with fallback and uncertainty) over a black-box model, so every number can be traced and questioned.
